Purpose The purpose of OMP 1 4 is to provide governance principles and high - level processes for the management of Qualification and interface d Certification and Acceptance activiti es, to enable OCCAR - EA to deliver the programme outputs as specified in the Prog ramme Decisions (ProgD) . The notions of Qualification, Certification and Acceptance are in accordance with th eir definitions as per Annex A of this document. Scope OMP 1 4 applies to all new OCCAR - managed Programmes 1 where development activities are carried - out and, if beneficial, to ne w elements of existing OCCAR - managed Programmes. It is to be considered by OCCAR Programme Divisions (PD), or by Programme Integration Teams (PIT). It provides the principles and procedure for the management of Qualification and interfaced activities (Cer tification and Acceptance) , to be applied to both the Product and its support systems. For programmes based on Commercial Off - The - Shelf (COTS) /No Development Items (NDI) products, it is assumed that a design fulfilling PS requirements with no or little adaptations needed is already available at the outset of the programme , so that OMP 14 may be applicable only for those sub - projects within the programme where significant design works remain necessary. However, being part of an international cooperation, it is essential that PSs define a set - up based on economy of effort and cooperation. To do so, PS s shall commit to the following principles in the ProgD : Each Nation is responsible for the regulation of its own Products . As a result, all C ertification activities within OCCAR PS s are conducted and regulated on a national basis. To minimise time, cost and any associated delay risks, it is essential that PS s reach agreement on the fundamental certification principles. Acceptance activities As a general principle, the availability of a Qualified Design (see Annex B , Step 3 ) is a pre - requisite to conduct Individual Acceptances 5 , unless otherwise settled with the PSs . The purpose of the Individual Acceptance step is to verify that each individual series production item meets the contractual requirements using the agreed acceptance criteria. The individual item acceptance will be based on a Certificate of Conformity ( CoC) or equivalent document and the assessment of the Acceptance tests and, if Certification is a pre - requisite to delivery, on a formal certification document as detailed in the contract. The acceptance tests should be tailored to each specific Product ty pe and define the relevant level of testing (e.g. individual test for aircraft, tests on samples only for munitions , submarine campaigns, sea trials, ... ). Governmental Quality Assurance (GQA) activities as required within the Product Acceptance process wi ll be performed by the GQAR in accordance with OMP 7. 7.
